description:
No spec subject

Review security M1 (calibrated M). Store.safe_decode/read paths, spec.triangle tracer-manifest read (spec.triangle.ex:132-140), and coverage_closure decode :erlang.binary_to_term without [:safe] — atom-exhaustion/ETF-bomb DoS from a hostile committed artifact. Bounded (consumers sit downstream of code execution the operator controls) but the fix is one word at each site; keep non-safe only where decoding must resurrect module atoms and document why (MfaKey atoms come via String.to_atom separately — see idioms M3 for the to_existing_atom variant).

comments.text:
CONTRACT (orchestrator-synthesized)

Context: your base is epic HEAD b5ea42b5ed168e23852ebe43d207a6f81bc54234, which includes specled_-q6l.1 (envelope loading consolidated into Store.load/1 — the decode sites may have moved relative to the ticket's original line numbers) and specled_-q6l.3 (v1 CoverageClosure.build/2 deleted). Re-locate the decode sites in the current tree before editing.

Allowed touches:
- lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex (safe_decode/read paths)
- lib/mix/tasks/spec.triangle.ex (tracer-manifest read, originally ~:132-140)
- lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex (only if a binary_to_term site still lives there after the .1 consolidation)
- test/** (targeted tests proving hostile-artifact rejection where cheap to add)
- .spec/specs/** ONLY if the spec gate demands subject co-change
- .spec/state.json, .spec/realization_hashes.json (tool-managed; regenerate only)

Out of Scope (files): mix.exs, .github/**, all other lib/**.

Out of Scope (intent): per the epic triage this is NOT a one-word fix — the tracer manifest and store hold atoms not guaranteed interned, so a blind [:safe] everywhere can break legitimate decodes. Do a per-site analysis: add [:safe] where the decoded term's atoms are guaranteed already-interned; where decoding must resurrect module atoms, keep non-safe and document why in a comment at the site (MfaKey atoms come via String.to_atom separately — see the review's idioms M3 note re the to_existing_atom variant, but do NOT change MfaKey semantics in this ticket). No behavior change for well-formed artifacts. No new deps.

Verification:
1. Per-site decision table in the completion record: every :erlang.binary_to_term call site in the touched files, with safe/non-safe decision + one-line rationale each.
2. Targeted tests green for every touched module (store_test, spec_triangle_test, coverage_closure_test as applicable); add at least one test proving an artifact with a never-interned atom is rejected (or classified :invalid_artifact) at a site you made safe.
3. mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix format --check-formatted.
4. mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base b5ea42b5ed168e23852ebe43d207a6f81bc54234 (base-pinned; ignore default origin/main drift).

  - shared private helper hostile_atom_binary/1: builds ETF bytes for a caller-supplied term containing a guaranteed-never-interned atom, by patching raw bytes into a same-length placeholder encoding (never calls String.to_atom on the hostile name itself)
Verification stubs flipped: none (no spec subject on this ticket)
Verification tier: change-scoped — test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs (25->27 tests), test/mix/tasks/spec_triangle_test.exs, test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs, test/specled_ex/coverage/aggregate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_cover_test_test.exs (63 tests total, 0 failures); mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; mix format --check-formatted clean; mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base b5ea42b5ed168e23852ebe43d207a6f81bc54234 status=pass errors=0 warnings=0 (branch-guard cross-cutting findings resolved via a Spec-Drift trailer on the commit, since this is a security hardening fix with no behavior change and no spec subject). Full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI.
Final-tier runs: 2 (both green)
Per-site decision table:
  - lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex:66 (Store.read/1, v1 bare-list decode): [:safe] — only atoms are this module's own fixed record keys (:test_id, :file, :lines_hit, :tags, :test_pid), always interned; this function is not on the production read path (only write_v2/read_v2/load are), so hardening it cannot regress a live consumer.
  - lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex:189 (read_v2/1, via safe_decode/2 with opts=[]): non-safe, documented at site — aggregate-mode envelope :files entries carry a raw :module atom (SpecLedEx.Coverage.Aggregate.analyse_lines/2) that CoverageTriangulation reads downstream (Enum.group_by(files, &Map.get(&1, :module))); mix spec.cover.ingest exists precisely to accept a .coverdata captured in another run/session, and a merged-in-place envelope can legitimately reference a module renamed/deleted since capture.
  - lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex:242 (read_status/1, via safe_decode/2 with opts=[:safe]): [:safe] — the last_run.status sidecar only ever holds {:ok, envelope_stats} (fixed keys, :aggregate/:per_test, integers, a DateTime struct) or {:refused, fixed_atom_reason}; never a project- or foreign-module atom.
  - lib/mix/tasks/spec.triangle.ex:117 (load_tracer_edges/0): non-safe, documented at site — Tracer merges the xref manifest incrementally and can legitimately retain "ghost" caller/callee entries for modules renamed/deleted since they were traced; per the Tracer's own moduledoc, read-time filtering (not decode) is the authoritative prune, so a fresh BEAM not yet holding that atom must still be able to decode the entry.
  - lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:43 (load_tracer_edges/0, duplicate of the above): non-safe, documented at site — same rationale, mirrors spec.triangle by design.
Deferred must requirements: none

Summary: Hardened the four :erlang.binary_to_term call sites the ticket named against atom-exhaustion DoS from a hostile committed artifact, via per-site analysis rather than a blanket [:safe]. Two sites (Store.read/1, Store.read_status/1) only ever decode atoms this module already owns or fixed status vocabulary, so they got [:safe]; two sites (Store.read_v2/1's envelope decode, and both load_tracer_edges/0 tracer-manifest readers) must legitimately be able to resurrect project module atoms that may not yet be interned in a fresh BEAM, so they stay non-safe with a comment documenting why. Added tests proving a hostile artifact carrying a never-interned atom is rejected at both hardened sites without the attacker-chosen atom ever getting interned. MfaKey's String.to_atom path was left untouched, out of scope.
